name: Supplementarity
summary: Two Z-states with antipodal phases α and α+π plugged into the same X-spider merge into one Z-spider with phase 2α+π.
description:
Two arity-one Z-spiders whose phases differ by π (they are *antipodal*) and that are connected to the same X-spider can be merged into a single Z-spider with phase $2\alpha+\pi$, connected to the X-spider by two wires. Both sides denote the state $\frac{1}{\sqrt2}(1-e^{2i\alpha})\ket{0}$. By the [Hopf rule](../hopf/) the right-hand side can be simplified further to a scalar times a phase-free X-state.

Supplementarity was introduced by Perdrix and Wang, inspired by an observation of Coecke and Edwards, who proved that it is *necessary*: it can be derived from the original rules of the ZX-calculus if and only if $\alpha$ is a multiple of $\pi/2$. In particular it cannot be derived for $\alpha=\pi/4$, which showed that the ZX-calculus of that time was incomplete for Clifford+T. It is one of the axioms of the complete axiomatisations of Jeandel, Perdrix and Vilmart for Clifford+T and for the full (universal) ZX-calculus. In Vilmart's near-minimal axiomatisation it is no longer an axiom, but is derived from the [Euler-angle rule](../euler-angles/).

Its graphical meaning is that *antiphase twins* can be merged, see [merging antiphase twins](../antiphase-twins/), and it is the case $n=2$ of [cyclotomic supplementarity](../cyclotomic-supplementarity/).
